title: Cost + Latency landscape: quickscan — quantized vs hybrid routing
body:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic benchmark note to capture early numbers and qualitative observations comparing: (A) heavy quantization-only model variants (4-bit / 8-bit FTQ style) vs (B) hybrid routing where requests are routed to a small pool of FP16/FP32 instances for long sequences and quantized instances for short sequences. Goal: identify immediate product guidance (default model selection and routing heuristics) for Optimize recommendations and the Console ‘model profile’ starter template.

Background / motivation:
- Teams want low unit cost without degrading tail latency for interactive apps (assistant/chat + code completion).
- Quantization reduces memory and per-token compute but can increase per-token latency variability and sometimes quality regressions.
- Hybrid routing is promising: keep a small warm FP pool to handle heavy tails and route most traffic to quantized fleet. Need numbers to justify default policy.

Experiment setup (quickscan):
- Model family: open-llm-xl-v1 (baseline FP16), quant-xl-4bit and quant-xl-8bit.
- HW: A100 80GB (FP pool) and A10G equivalent (quant pool) fashion; both on Redwood Dedicated env.
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes:
  1) short-chat: median tokens per request = 24, 95p = 56
  2) mixed-assistant: median = 72, 95p = 420 (heavy tails)
  3) long-session: median = 320, 95p = 900
- Arrival pattern: Poisson with mean rate scaled to achieve ~70% utilization on quant pool in isolation.
- Metrics collected: p50, p90, p95 latency (generate completion), tokens/sec, token-cost-est (infra/$), %requests routed to FP pool, quality quick check (embedding similarity vs FP baseline on small eval set).
- Duration: 2h per scenario with steady-state window last 60m used for numbers.

Text charts (ASCII) — key numbers (rounded):
Scenario A: short-chat (mostly short)
Config | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | tokens/sec | $/k tokens (relative) | routed_to_FP% | quality_delta
quant-4bit | 45 | 140 | 1,200 | 0.42x | 3% | -0.7 pts
quant-8bit | 38 | 130 | 1,100 | 0.55x | 2% | -0.2 pts
FP16-only | 32 | 120 | 950 | 1x | 0% | 0 pts
Hybrid (q4 main, FP on tail) | 34 | 125 | 1,150 | 0.48x | 8% | -0.1 pts

Scenario B: mixed-assistant (heavy tails)
Config | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | tokens/sec | $/k tokens (relative) | routed_to_FP% | quality_delta
quant-4bit | 62 | 820 | 600 | 0.40x | 22% | -1.6 pts
quant-8bit | 55 | 740 | 560 | 0.53x | 18% | -0.6 pts
FP16-only | 48 | 360 | 450 | 1x | 0% | 0 pts
Hybrid | 50 | 380 | 520 | 0.62x | 30% | -0.2 pts

Scenario C: long-session (mostly long)
Config | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | tokens/sec | $/k tokens (relative) | routed_to_FP% | quality_delta
quant-4bit | 120 | 1800 | 180 | 0.38x | 54% | -2.4 pts
quant-8bit | 105 | 1600 | 160 | 0.48x | 47% | -1.1 pts
FP16-only | 88 | 680 | 130 | 1x | 0% | 0 pts
Hybrid | 92 | 700 | 150 | 0.59x | 63% | -0.3 pts

Interpretation / quick takeaways:
- Cost: Quantized variants give ~40–60% nominal token-cost reduction in isolation (per-token compute), consistent with expectations.
- Latency: For short-chat, quantization is strictly beneficial (lower cost and comparable p95) — perfect candidate to default to quantized model.
- Tails: For mixed and long workloads, quantized-only fleets see p95 explode because long sequences saturate the quant pool and quant kernels are less efficient on very long sequences (KV cache / tiling inefficiencies). That drives % routed_to_FP rises in hybrid and also higher cost than naive per-token estimate.
- Hybrid routing: Hybrid reduces p95 significantly compared to quant-only in mixed/long scenarios while keeping most tokens on quant instances. Overall cost is ~60% of FP-only in hybrid case for mixed workloads — attractive.
- Quality: Small embedding similarity checks show quant-4bit sometimes has measurable quality drop (esp. long). quant-8bit is a better tradeoff for quality-sensitive apps. Hybrid preserves quality near baseline since many long requests get FP path.

Short ASCII plot (rough): fraction_routed_to_FP vs request_length (binned) — mixed-assistant
bins (tokens): 0-32 | 33-128 | 129-512 | 513+
quant-4bit routed%: 2% | 12% | 36% | 78%
quant-8bit routed%: 1% | 8% | 30% | 70%
hybrid routing policy observed routed%: 4% | 18% | 44% | 82%

Observations (practical):
- A naive per-token cost multiplier underestimates actual cost when tail routing increases FP usage; product guidance must account for routed_to_FP uplift.
- For interactive low-latency products (chat widgets), default to quant-8bit unless customers opt-in for max quality. quant-4bit is cost-optimal only when tail mass is small and quality tolerance exists.
- Recommend shipping a default hybrid routing rule in Console: route to FP if request_token_count > 256 OR expected_completion_length_estimate > 512 OR observed cache-miss > X. (Need to define cache-miss metric).

Open questions / TODOs:
- We used synthetic mixes; need to rerun with sampled production traces (prod anonymized) to validate routed% numbers.
- Need a micro-eval on semantic tasks (qa, summarization) for quality delta beyond embedding similarity.
- Explore dynamic thresholding (learning threshold per-customer by A/B).
- Check kernel-level profiles: why are quant kernels slower on long sequences? Possible memory movement / tiling inefficiency — request SRE/serving-runtime to capture perf traces (GH#repo/serving-runtime/issues/210).

Guidance for product pages / Console UX (draft):
- In the model profile editor, expose: quantization level suggestion (4/8), expected tail behavior (low/med/high), and a recommended routing heuristic (token-threshold + warm-FP-reserve).
- Backfill tooltips: "Why hybrid? Hybrid holds a small warm FP pool to keep tails snappy while saving on per-token infra cost."
- Provide cost preview UI that shows 'estimated routed FP uplift' based on sample traffic (link to sampling job).

Appendix: quick quality note (embedding sim method)
- Method: 200 eval prompts spanning 3 tasks; compute cosine similarity of embedding for quant vs FP baseline using top-10 candidate completions. Reported quality_delta = FP_mean_sim - quant_mean_sim (higher = worse).

Immediate next steps (owners):
- prod-trace re-run: Jun Park (data access + sampling) — target week of 2026-12-06.
- Kernel traces + tiled memory profile: Evan Cole + serving-runtime eng — create perf capture ticket GH#repo/serving-runtime/issues/210 (blocked on infra).
- Expand quality eval to task-level metrics: Marisol Vega (small eval harness).
- Draft Console wording + default rule: Priya Raman — include cost-preview and toggles.

Notes to self: this is intentionally light — keep for the product briefing on Mon. Need clean charts and cost model numbers for slide deck; convert ASCII tables to real charts when we have prod traces.
